title: Postles v. Heritage Presbytery
disposition_detail: Complaint denied on the merits. The SJC rejected the challenges to the investigating committee's investigation and recommendation and to Heritage Presbytery's institution of process, including the alleged lack of a written report, departure from BCO 31-2, and non-BCO wording.
first_summary: The SJC denied a complaint challenging Heritage Presbytery’s November 12, 2016 decision to charge a teaching elder with violating ordination vows 6 and 7 and to appoint a prosecutor to investigate and, if necessary, indict. The Commission reasoned that the investigating committee merely recommended action, that no special authorization was constitutionally required for such a recommendation, and that the presbytery’s procedure substantially followed BCO 31-2 despite non-BCO wording and the absence of a written report.
summary: The SJC denied a complaint challenging Heritage Presbytery’s November 12, 2016 action charging a teaching elder with violating ordination vows 6 and 7 and appointing a prosecutor to investigate and, if necessary, indict. The complaint alleged the investigating committee lacked authority for judicial process, no written report existed, and the procedure and wording violated BCO 31-2. The Commission held a committee recommendation is not judicial action, no special instruction was required, the BCO 31-2 steps were followed, and the wording did not violate the accused’s rights.

evidence_notes.dispute: The complaint challenged HP’s Nov. 12, 2016 motion, made on the Ad Interim Committee’s recommendation, to charge the TE with violating Ordination Vows 6 and 7 and to appoint a prosecutor to investigate and, if necessary, prepare an indictment (lines 31–43, 53, 81–87).
evidence_notes.outcomes_and_reasons: The SJC answered the issue “No” and denied the complaint (lines 57–59, 111). It held the committee’s investigation and recommendation were not judicial action and no special instruction was required (lines 67–73); HP followed BCO 31-2’s investigation, strong-presumption, and prosecutor-appointment steps (lines 83, 91–109); no written report was constitutionally required (line 91); and the non-BCO wording did not violate the Constitution or the accused’s rights (lines 89–111).
evidence_notes.qualifications: RE Dailey requested removal of his name while the complaint was pending (line 47). The decision records concurring and dissenting votes without separate reasoning (lines 113–115), including five dissents and two absences (line 115).
evidence_notes.incorporated_decisions: No decision is incorporated by reference. The opinion cites Malone v. Metropolitan New York Presbytery (SJC 2007-02; M36GA2008, pp. 99–107) (line 71 and n.39) and Payne v. Western Carolina Presbytery (lines 106–109) as precedent.
